spots.name: Freedom Monument
spots.summary: The Freedom Monument is a monument located in Riga, Latvia, honouring soldiers killed during the Latvian War of Independence (1918–1920). It is considered an important symbol of the freedom, independence, and sovereignty of Latvia.

spots.name: Riga Cathedral
spots.summary: Riga Cathedral formally The Cathedral Church of Saint Mary, is the Evangelical Lutheran cathedral in Riga, Latvia. It is the seat of the Archbishop of Riga.

spots.name: St. Peter's Church
spots.summary: St. Peter's Church is a Lutheran church in Riga, the capital of Latvia, dedicated to Saint Peter. It is a parish church of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Latvia.

spots.name: Vecrīga
spots.summary: Vecrīga is the historical center and a neighbourhood of Riga, Latvia, located in the Central District on the east side of Daugava River. Vecrīga is famous for its old churches and cathedrals, such as Riga Cathedral, St. James's Cathedral and St. Peter's Church.

spots.name: Riga Radio and TV Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Riga Radio and TV Tower in Riga, Latvia is the tallest tower in the European Union. It is operated by the Latvian State Radio and Television Centre (LVRTC). It was built between 1979 and 1989 with funding from the central government of the Soviet Union.

spots.name: Riga Central Market

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Riga Central Market is Europe's largest market and bazaar in Riga, Latvia. It is one of the most notable structures from the 20th century in Latvia and has been included in the UNESCO World Heritage Site list together with Old Riga in 1998. It was planned from 1922 and built from 1924 to 1930.

spots.name: Three Brothers

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Three Brothers is a building complex consisting of three houses, situated in Riga, Latvia. The houses together form the oldest complex of dwelling houses in Riga. Each house represents various periods of development of dwelling house construction.

spots.name: Nativity Cathedral, Riga

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Nativity of Christ Cathedral, Riga, Latvia was built to a design by Nikolai Chagin and Robert Pflug in a Neo-Byzantine style between 1876 and 1883, with decorations made by the firm of August Volz, during the period when the country was part of the Russian Empire.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of the Nativity of Christ, Riga

spots.name: Riga Castle
spots.summary: Riga Castle is a castle on the banks of River Daugava in Riga, the capital of Latvia. The castle was founded in 1330. Its structure was thoroughly rebuilt between 1497 and 1515. Upon the castle's seizure by the Swedes, they constructed spacious annexes in 1641.

spots.name: St. James's Cathedral
spots.summary: St James's Cathedral is the Roman Catholic cathedral of Riga in Latvia. The cathedral is dedicated to Saint James the Greater. The building is part of the Old Riga UNESCO World Heritage Site and lies directly opposite the House of the Livonian Noble Corporation, the meeting place of Latvia's parliament the Saeima.

spots.name: Riga Ghetto
spots.summary: Riga Ghetto was a small area in Maskavas Forštate, a neighbourhood of Riga, Latvia, where Nazis forced Jews from Latvia, and later from the German "Reich", to live during World War II. On October 25, 1941, the Nazis evicted the ghetto's non-Jewish inhabitants and relocated all Jews from Riga and its vicinity there.

spots.name: Museum of the Occupation of Latvia

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of the Occupation of Latvia is a museum and history education institution in Riga, Latvia.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum of the Occupation of Latvia

spots.name: Albert Street
spots.summary: Albert Street is a street in central Riga known for its Art Nouveau buildings. It was built in 1901 and named after Bishop Albert, who founded Riga in 1201.

spots.name: Joom

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Joom is a group of e-commerce companies founded in Latvia in 2016 and headquartered in Lisbon, Portugal. It also has offices in China, Hong Kong, Brazil, the USA, Germany and Latvia. As of 2025, Joom consists of the following business units.

spots.name: St. John's Church

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: St. John's Church is a Lutheran church in Riga, the capital of Latvia. It is a parish church of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Latvia. The church is situated at the address 24 Skārņu Street.

photo.author: Christopher Walker from Krakow, Poland. Crop and rotation by User:Sozi

spots.name: Swedish Gate
spots.summary: The Swedish Gate is situated in Riga, Latvia, and was erected 1698 as a part of the Riga Wall to provide access to barracks outside the city wall. These gates are the only remaining gates from the former eight. They are located on Torņa street 11.

spots.name: Powder Tower

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Powder Tower is situated in Riga, Latvia, and originally a part of the defensive system of the town. The current Powder Tower was built in 1650 and renovated in the years 1937 to 1940 when it was added to the structure of the Latvian War Museum.

spots.name: House of the Livonian Noble Corporation
spots.summary: The House of the Livonian Noble Corporation, also known as Saeima House, is the seat of the parliament of Latvia, the Saeima. It is located in the Vecpilsēta neighbourhood of downtown Riga.
spots.wikipediaTitle: House of the Livonian Noble Corporation

spots.name: Vanšu Bridge
spots.summary: The Vanšu Bridge in Riga is a cable-stayed bridge that crosses the Daugava river in Riga, the capital of Latvia. The word vanšu refers to the cables suspending its deck, comparing them to nautical rigging also known as shrouds in English; thus a direct translation of the name is Shroud Bridge.

spots.name: National Library of Latvia

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Library of Latvia, originally known as the State Library of Latvia, is a national cultural institution under the supervision of the Ministry of Culture of Latvia. Its current main building is known as the Castle of Light.

spots.name: Railway Bridge, Riga
spots.summary: The Railway Bridge is a bridge that crosses the Daugava river in Riga, the capital of Latvia.

spots.name: Corner House
spots.summary: The Corner House is a historic building in the city center of Riga, Latvia. It was known as the headquarters of the Soviet KGB in Latvia from 1940 to 1941 and from 1944 to 1991. The official address is 61 Brīvības iela.

spots.name: Riga Motor Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Riga Motor Museum is the biggest antique vehicle museum in the Baltic countries, located in Riga, Latvia. The museum is a state agency operating under the Republic of Latvia Ministry of Transport.

spots.name: Bikernieki Memorial
spots.summary: Biķernieki Memorial is a war memorial to the Holocaust victims of World War II in Biķernieki forest in Riga, Latvia.

spots.name: Peitav Synagogue

hours.note: Closed Mon, Wed, Sun

spots.summary: The Peitav Synagogue or Peitav-Shul is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 6/8 Pietavas Street, Vecrīga, in Riga, Latvia.

spots.name: Our Lady of Sorrows Church

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Our Lady of Sorrows Church is a Roman Catholic church in Riga, the capital of Latvia. The church is situated at the address 5 Pils Street. It was built in 1785.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Our Lady of Sorrows Church, Riga

spots.name: Laima Clock
spots.summary: The Laima Clock is a landmark in central Riga, Latvia. Its location between the Old Town and the Centre commercial district has made it a landmark of the city.

spots.name: St. Gertrude Old Church

hours.note: Closed Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat

spots.summary: St Gertrude Old Church is a Lutheran church in Riga, the capital of Latvia. It is a parish church of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Latvia. The church is situated at the address 8 Ģertrūdes Street. It has a long association with Riga's German ethnic community, and the congregation worship in the German language.

spots.name: St. George's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. George's Church used to be a Catholic church in Riga, the capital of Latvia. The church building now houses the Latvian Museum of Decorative Arts and Design and is situated at the address 10/12 Skārņu Street. It is the oldest stone building in Riga as well as the first church constructed in Riga.

spots.name: Bastejkalns Park
spots.summary: Bastejkalns Park is a spacious park on the northern edge of the old town of Latvian capital Riga.

spots.name: St. Saviour's Church, Riga

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Saviour's Church is a congregation of the Church of England in Riga, Latvia. Its parish church is located at Anglikāņu iela 2. This is to the north of the old town centre (Vecrīga), close to Riga Castle and the banks of the Daugava River.

spots.name: St. Mary Magdalene's Church
spots.summary: St. Mary Magdalene's Church is a Roman Catholic church in Riga, the capital of Latvia. The church is situated at the address 2 Klostera iela.

spots.name: Kaļķu iela
spots.summary: Kaļķu iela is a street in the medieval old town of Riga, Latvia. The street begins at the central square Rātslaukums and goes to the North East as far as the boundary of the historical centre. Brīvības iela and Brīvības bulvāris form a continuation of Kaļķu iela.

spots.name: Brīvības iela
spots.summary: Brīvības iela is the central street of Riga, the capital and most populous city of Latvia. It is more than 12 km long, cutting across all of Riga, from the historical centre to the outskirts and the city limits.

spots.name: Riga Zoo
spots.summary: Riga Zoo is a city-owned zoo in Riga, Latvia. It is located in Mežaparks neighbourhood next to the Mežaparks park, on the western bank of Ķīšezers lake. Riga Zoo houses around 4000 animals of nearly 500 species and is visited by 250–300,000 visitors annually.

spots.name: Convent Yard, Riga
spots.summary: The Convent Yard is situated in Riga, Latvia, and originates from the first half of the 13th century. It is some of the oldest part of Riga that has been preserved.

spots.name: Akmens tilts
spots.summary: Stone Bridge is a bridge over the Daugava River in Riga, Latvia. It was called the October Bridge until 1992.

spots.name: Holy Trinity Orthodox Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Holy Trinity Orthodox Church is an Eastern Orthodox church in Riga, the capital of Latvia. The church is situated in Pārdaugava at the address 2 Meža Street.

spots.name: Zunda Towers

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Zunda Towers are a pair of skyscrapers in Riga, Latvia. The buildings were designed by Latvian architectural firm F.L.Tadao & Lukševics, while the façade was designed by architect Helmut Jahn. Both towers have a mix of office space and residential units.

spots.name: Vērmane Garden
spots.summary: Vērmane Garden is the oldest public garden in the city of Riga, Latvia, and currently comprises an area of approximately 5 hectares. The current name is a Latvian transliteration of the garden's original German name.

spots.name: Latvian Museum of Decorative Arts and Design

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Latvian Museum of Decorative Arts and Design is an arts museum in Riga, Latvia. The museum was established on 1 January 1989 and opened to the public on 6 July 1989. It is located in the former church St. George's Church, Riga, the oldest surviving stone building in Riga.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Latvian Museum of Decorative Arts and Design

spots.name: Great Choral Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Great Choral Synagogue was a Jewish congregation and synagogue, that was located on Gogoļa iela, in the Latgale neighborhood of Riga, Latvia. Designed by Paul von Hardenack in predominately Renaissance Revival style, the synagogue was completed in 1871.

spots.name: Mežaparks
spots.summary: Mežaparks is a neighbourhood of Northern District in Riga, the capital of Latvia. It consists of a residential area to the South and a large urban park to the North of the same name – Mežaparks. The neighbourhood is located on the western shore of Lake Ķīšezers. The name is literally translated as "forest park".

spots.name: Great Cemetery
spots.summary: The Great Cemetery was formerly the principal cemetery of Riga in Latvia, established in 1773. It was the main burial ground of the Baltic Germans in Latvia.

spots.name: St. Alexander Nevsky Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Alexander Nevsky Church is an Eastern Orthodox church in Riga, the capital of Latvia. The church is situated at the address 56 Brīvības Street.

spots.name: Annunciation of Our Most Holy Lady Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Annunciation of Our Most Holy Lady Church is an Orthodox church in Riga, the capital of Latvia. The church is situated at the address 9 Emilijas Benjamiņas Street.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Annunciation of Our Most Holy Lady Church, Riga

spots.name: Latvian Museum of Natural History

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Latvian National Museum of Natural History is a natural history museum in Riga, Latvia. It was founded in 1845 as the Riga Naturalist Society.

spots.name: Grebenstchikov House of Prayer, Riga

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Grebenstchikov House of Prayer is an Old Believers place of worship in Riga, the capital of Latvia. It is situated at the address Mazā Krasta iela 73.

spots.name: St. Francis Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Francis Church is a Roman Catholic church in Riga, the capital of Latvia. The church is situated at the address 16 Katoļu Street in the Maskavas Forštate neighborhood. The building was consecrated in 1892 by Franciszek Albin Symon, the auxiliary bishop of Mohilev.

spots.name: St. Catherine's Roman Catholic Church, Riga

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Catherine's Roman Catholic Church was a catholic church in Riga, the capital of Latvia. The church was situated at the address 9/11 Šķūņu Street.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St. Catherine's Roman Catholic Church, Riga

spots.name: Āgenskalns Market

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Āgenskalns Market is the oldest marketplace on the left bank of Daugava in Riga. Āgenskalns Market’s building is one of the examples of 20th-century rational Art Nouveau.

spots.name: Church of Jesus

hours.note: Closed Mon, Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Church of Jesus is a Lutheran church in Riga, the capital of Latvia. It is a parish church of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Latvia. The church is situated at the address 18 Elijas Street.

spots.name: Victory Park
spots.summary: Victory Park is a park in Riga, located on the left bank of the Daugava, in the district of Āgenskalns. The modern area of the park is 36.7 hectares.

spots.name: Žanis Lipke Memorial

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Žanis Lipke Memorial is a memorial museum located on the island of Ķīpsala in Riga, Latvia, at Mazais Balasta dambis, 9. It was opened in 2012 next to the former home of rescuer of Jews Žanis Lipke, where he had arranged a shelter for rescued Jews from the Riga Ghetto during World War II.

spots.name: Church of Luther

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Church of Luther, or Torņakalns Church after its geographical location in Torņakalns, is a Lutheran church in Riga, the capital of Latvia. It is a parish church of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Latvia. The church is situated at the address 3/5 Torņakalns Street.

spots.name: Arsenāls – Fine Arts Museum
spots.summary: Arsenāls – Fine Arts Museum is an art museum in Riga, Latvia, department of the Latvian National Museum of Art.

spots.name: Pushkin Statue
spots.summary: The Pushkin Statue in Kronvalds Park in Riga, Latvia, was erected in 2009 as a gift from the city of Moscow and removed in 2023. It was made by sculptor Alexander Tartynov.

spots.name: Citadel of Riga
spots.summary: The Citadel of Riga was a fortress in Riga, located near the Old Town, existing from the 17th to 19th centuries. It provided additional defense for the city and served as a base for the city garrison. It was heavily damaged during the Siege of Riga by the forces of Peter I in 1709 and was repeatedly rebuilt.

spots.name: Kalpaka Boulevard Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kalpaka Boulevard Library is a branch of the University of Latvia libraries located on its eponymous street in central Riga, Latvia. It is housed in a historic mansion built between 1874 and 1878 to designs of Jānis Frīdrihs Baumanis.

spots.name: St. Paul's Lutheran Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Paul's Lutheran Church is a Lutheran church in Riga, the capital of Latvia. It is a parish church of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Latvia. The church is situated at the address 1 Augusta Deglava Street.

spots.name: Museum of the History of Riga and Navigation
spots.summary: Actually two museums plus a number of special exhibits, though you pay one price. English, German and Russian descriptions of each permanent collections are provided in a booklet inside each exhibit hall. Both of the main museums are quite interesting, and they provide a good idea of what Riga was like in the past.

spots.name: The House of the Black Cat
spots.summary: This building (also housing a pub of no particular note) is most famous for the two statues of black cats on the roofs. The legend has it that a disgruntled tradesman who was not accepted into the Big Guild, built this house and put the cats on it with their tails pointing towards the Big Guild, thus expressing his scorn.

spots.name: Triangula Bastion
spots.summary: A modern building with an excavated fragment of the historical fortification wall system along the river. The building has the best view terraces in Riga.

spots.name: Literature and music museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: For about 50 years it was a large union of memorial houses devoted to a range of writers. The latest reorganisation in 2009 has resulted in more simple and recognizable establishment – Literature and Music Museum.

spots.name: Art gallery "Jēkabs"

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Jēkabs art gallery offers exhibitions and fine art auctions.

spots.name: Esplanade Park
spots.summary: Designed by Georg Kuphaldt, who was expelled by Germany in 1915 as a spy because he had a telescope in his garden.

spots.name: House of Dannenstern
spots.summary: The house was built by and is named after Ernst Metue von Dannenstern.

spots.name: Red warehouses

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A huge cluster of mid-19th century warehouses between the train station and Central Market. They remind of the former trade harbor.

spots.name: Sun Museum
spots.summary: One of Riga's weirdest museums, it covers the history of sun mythology and its role in Latvian culture.

spots.name: Latvian National Museum of Art

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Latvian National Museum of Art is the most significant depository in the nation for works of art.

spots.name: National Museum of Art

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Latvian National Museum of Art is the most significant depository in the nation for works of art. Houses many works by Latvian artists.

spots.summary: The collection covers the period from 1945 to 1991 in Latvia.
